title: Gaze_Behaviours_of_Elite_Ice_Hockey_Play
universal_lens: Gaze behavior in tactical sports maps to perceptual-motor feedback loops with variable F/T dynamics based on spatial and temporal context. Eye-tracking frequency\/time dynamics during elite vs non-elite defensive play mapped via Bayesian decision-making kernels.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian inference models F/T patterns as evidence streams for tactical decision-making under uncertainty in real-time team sports environments. GSI infers cognitive load and attention allocation through gaze-based temporal sequences using conformal predictive models of plus-minus performance differentials.
gse_mapping: Situational reasoning engine encodes gaze-driven state transitions via dynamic fixation-tracking profiles to predict and simulate player actions. GSE encodes situational awareness transitions across PR-SA-DM phases via dynamic state-space representations of gaze-in-action trajectories.

primitives.name: Fixation and Tracking Dynamics
primitives.verbatim_quote: Research in tactical sports has found conflicting results, with some studies finding a high frequency and low duration of F/T while others have found the opposite - a low frequency and long duration of F/T.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'f': 'frequency of fixation events per second (Hz)', 't': 'duration of each fixation in seconds (s)'}
primitives.assumptions: F/T behavior varies inversely with spatial complexity and temporal pressure in tactical settings.
primitives.breakdown_regime: At extreme distances or low visibility, F/T becomes highly frequent but brief.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's probabilistic cue detection and GSE's attention allocation algorithms.
layer2.telemetry: Eye-tracking data from video analysis of player gaze during live plays.

primitives.name: Contextual Gaze Modulation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Irrespective of expertise, the context of the tactical play was a factor in determining the frequency and relative duration of F/T.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'C': 'tactical context variable (dimensionless)', 'f_C': 'context-adjusted fixation frequency (Hz)', 't_C': 'context-adjusted fixation duration (s)'}
primitives.assumptions: Tactical context directly influences gaze strategy through cognitive load modulation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When C approaches zero (static), f_C increases and t_C decreases.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE's contextual state-space model and GSI's belief updating framework.

primitives.name: Spatial Scanning Efficiency
primitives.verbatim_quote: When the tactical problem was lcoated further from the athlete, then a high frequency and low duration of F/T were found due to the necessity of scanning a wider field of view.
primitives.assumptions: Scanning efficiency scales inversely with spatial extent of visual field.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's spatial attention kernel and GSI's visual field coverage estimator.

primitives.name: Temporal Attention Shift
primitives.verbatim_quote: As the play progressed, a lower frequency and longer duration of F/T were found due to the decrease in the distance between the participant and opposing players and the more specific 1 on 1 role assumed at the end of each play.
primitives.assumptions: Attention narrows over time as spatial resolution increases.
primitives.breakdown_regime: As t_p → final stage, f_t → 0 and t_t → max.

layer2.mapping: Reflects GSE's temporal state transition logic and GSI's sequential decision tree.

primitives.name: Eye Tracking Frequency/Time Dynamics
primitives.verbatim_quote: The goal of this pilot study was therefore to determine the F/T of E and NE athletes during defensive plays performed on ice.
primitives.assumptions: Gaze behavior follows deterministic temporal patterns under controlled sport environments; F/T correlates with decision accuracy.
primitives.breakdown_regime: At zero gaze fixation, F/T becomes undefined due to lack of measurable visual engagement.

layer2.mapping: Maps gaze frequency and duration to cognitive processing states within decision-making frameworks of GSI.
layer2.telemetry: Temporal sequence of fixations per second during defensive actions.

primitives.name: Plus-Minus Performance Metric
primitives.verbatim_quote: The plus-minus score is a standard measure used in ice hockey that is calculated by subtracting the number of goals scored when a player's line is on the ice from the number scored by the opponents.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'PM': 'plus-minus score (dimensionless)', 'G_{\\text{own}}': 'goals scored by own team (integer)', 'G_{\\text{opp}}': 'goals scored by opponent team (integer)'}
primitives.assumptions: Performance is linearly correlated with team-level goal differential during active play periods.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When both teams score equal goals, PM approaches zero; negative values indicate poor defensive contribution.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphically maps PM to GSI's probabilistic model of success likelihood in defensive scenarios.
layer2.telemetry: Cumulative goal differential over multiple game segments.

primitives.name: Temporal Phase Structure
primitives.verbatim_quote: The gaze image (left) shows the field of view in front of the athlete and location of the gaze in the hockey environment as indicated by the white cursor.
primitives.assumptions: Each phase exhibits distinct gaze behavior profiles; transitions between phases are marked by specific temporal thresholds.

primitives.name: Gaze Field of View Mapping
primitives.verbatim_quote: The frequency, duration, location and temporal sequence of F/T was determined during the execution of successful (plus) and unsuccessful (minus) defeisnive plays which were skated against opponents who played at the same competitive level.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'FOV': 'field of view (radians)', 'G': 'gaze position vector (meters)', 'P': 'player position vector (meters)'}
primitives.assumptions: Visual attention aligns with spatial proximity to key game elements such as puck, opponents, teammates.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Gaze deviation beyond FOV boundary indicates loss of situational awareness.

layer2.mapping: Maps gaze coordinates to GSE’s environmental state representation using geometric transformations.

primitives.name: Phase Transition Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: The temporal onset and offset of each phase were defined by constant events signalling the transition from the PR to SA to DM phase.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \mathcal{T}_{\tau} (dimensionless transition operator), \Omega_{t} (temporal domain in seconds), \Sigma (discrete phase state space)
primitives.assumptions: Phase transitions are deterministic functions of specific biomechanical or kinematic events; time is discretized by video frame rate.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs if event signals are occluded or simultaneous, rendering the mapping \mathcal{T}_{\tau} non-injective.

layer2.mapping: Directly maps to the GSE state-transition kernel, defining the exact boundaries for situational reasoning modules.
layer2.telemetry: Frame-accurate timestamps of phase onset and offset extracted via shuttle control.

primitives.name: Fixation Tracking Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: F/T gaze were defined using minimum duration parameters from the eye movement literature (Carpenter, 1988) and occurred when the gaze was stable on a location, object, player or players for a minimum of 99.9 ms (3 or more frames).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \Delta t (duration in milliseconds), \tau_{min} = 99.9 \text{ ms}, v_{gaze} (angular velocity in degrees/s), \epsilon (stability threshold)
primitives.assumptions: Saccadic suppression is negligible; stability implies zero angular velocity within sensor noise bounds.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down under extreme head acceleration where vestibular-ocular reflex overrides standard saccadic models.

layer2.mapping: Forms the foundational feature extraction layer for GSI's conformal scoring, filtering high-frequency noise from raw eye-tracking data.
layer2.telemetry: Binary classification of gaze frames into F/T vs. saccade based on 3-frame stability.

primitives.name: Spatial Gaze Manifold
primitives.verbatim_quote: The approximate location of F/T on the ice during the PR, SA and DM phases is shown by the shaded portions of Figure 2.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: L_{F/T} (set of spatial coordinates in meters), \mathcal{M}_{ice} (2D Riemannian manifold of the rink), \Sigma_{phase} (current phase state)
primitives.assumptions: The ice surface is a flat Euclidean plane locally; gaze locations map directly to world coordinates.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Coordinate mapping fails if camera calibration drifts or if perspective projection introduces severe parallax errors.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE's spatial awareness grid, allowing the engine to weight specific zones based on historical fixation density.
layer2.telemetry: Centroid coordinates of shaded regions in Figure 2 mapped to rink X-Y axes.

primitives.name: Temporal Sequence Metric
primitives.verbatim_quote: Frequency of F/T was determined, as was the relative duration (%) and temporal order of F/T in each phase (F/T1, F/T2...F/Tn).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: N (count of fixations, dimensionless), \Delta t_i (duration in ms), T_{total} (phase duration in ms), \pi (permutation vector representing order)
primitives.assumptions: The sequence of fixations forms a Markovian chain; relative duration normalizes for varying play speeds.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Metric becomes ill-defined if T_{total} approaches zero or if N exceeds computational memory bounds for permutation tracking.

layer2.mapping: Supplies the sequential feature vector to GSI's Bayesian updater, enabling comparison of temporal ordering between Elite and Non-Elite agents.
layer2.telemetry: Ordered list of fixation durations and their normalized percentages per phase.

primitives.name: Temporal Gaze Economy
primitives.verbatim_quote: Overall, the E player was more economical in his use of F/T, using fewer F/T of longer duration compared to the NE.
primitives.assumptions: Fixation duration T follows exponential decay with increasing tactical complexity; expert athletes show reduced F/T count but increased mean duration.
primitives.breakdown_regime: At onset of SA phase, T decreases rapidly due to high spatial entropy; at later phases, T stabilizes with decreasing inter-player distances.

layer2.mapping: Gaze economy maps to information processing efficiency in GSI; in GSE, it defines optimal decision-making time windows for role transitions.
layer2.telemetry: Mean F/T duration per trial, count of fixations per second

primitives.name: Spatial Fixation Cluster

primitives.name: Tactical Phase Duration

primitives.assumptions: F/T duration is proportional to cognitive load; percentage normalization enables cross-player comparison.

primitives.name: Gaze Transition Sequence

reasoning_traces.think: The mathematical derivation of elite performance in this chapter window rests upon the rigorous partitioning of continuous time into discrete cognitive-motor phases: Preparation (PR), Search/Analysis (SA), and Decision/Movement (DM). We model the ice rink as a two-dimensional Riemannian manifold \mathcal{M}_{ice}. The defender's gaze trajectory \gamma(t) is a stochastic curve over this manifold. The primitive 'phase_transition_operator' acts as a discontinuous mapping \mathcal{T}_{\tau}, triggered by specific kinematic thresholds (e.g., first skating movement). This creates a piecewise definition of the agent's state. Within the SA phase, the 'fixation_tracking_kernel' filters the raw derivative of \gamma(t), isolating points where angular velocity drops below \epsilon for \tau \ge 99.9 ms. These isolated points constitute the 'spatial_gaze_manifold', effectively reducing the infinite-dimensional path space to a finite set of salient coordinates L_{F/T}. The 'temporal_sequence_metric' then imposes an ordered topology on these coordinates, generating a vector \Psi that encapsulates both the frequency and the relative duration of information sampling. The core epistemic insight is that elite status is not merely a function of spatial accuracy, but of the temporal optimization of \Psi. The Elite player minimizes redundant sampling (lower N) while maximizing the informational yield per unit time (higher relative duration on critical cues). This transforms the qualitative observation of 'better vision' into a quantifiable deviation in the distribution of \Psi between Elite and Non-Elite populations, forming the basis for subsequent Bayesian inference in GSI.

The system must strictly isolate the cognitive sampling phase from the physical execution phase to maintain the integrity of the Bayesian updates in GSI.
